title.narrative: DRC PCJR 2024-2026 (Lead)

description.narrative: The DRC PCJR 2024-2026 JR 2024-2026 focuses on North and South Kivu provinces, based on the highest needs in the country. The main objective of the 13 partners in the DRC JR is to collaboratively address the direct needs and relieve the suffering of the most vulnerable people, particularly IDPs and host communities, through a multi-sectoral approach covering WASH, Education, Protection, FSL and MPCA activities. The DRC JR focuses on the territories of Masisi and Lubero in North Kivu and on Kalehe and Fizi territories in South Kivu. Within the administrative zone of territories, the JR targets 4 health zones (HZ).

The DRCJR 2024-2026 will be implemented across four territories and six health zones in North Kivu and South Kivu with a total reach of 412.530 beneficiaries. The target group are the individuals affected by conflict. This includes, IDPs, returnees and host communities.

The Joint Response provides Food Security activities in most of the health zones. Education is promoted through WASH facilities in schools and snacks provided during catch-up classes. Child-Friendly Spaces will be created for play opportunities for children. This is for a multi-sectoral response. MPCA will be done in 1 health zone.

title.narrative: WSH-R2 Excreta disposal

description.narrative: Access: ratio (user/facility) of 1 toilet for a max. 20 people, distance < 50 metres from dwellings, or as locally agreed. Clean: regular cleaning and maintenance for public facilities.Dignified: Use of toilets respect cultural preference and is arranged by household(s) and/or segregated by sex. Unsafe facilities: unstable (unlined) pits with risk of collapse, pits accessible to vectors, pits contaminating water tables and poorly sited facilities which expose women and girls to attacks, especially at night. Functional facility: fully constructed, in working order and properly maintained, of a type and in a location acceptable to intended users, with hand washing facilities and anal cleansing material.

title.narrative: PRO-R8 Support to separated/unaccompanied children

description.narrative: "1) Care arrangements can include temporary care arrangements in host family or other care arrangements.2) Appropriate means (but is not limited to) that care arrangements must take into account different needs of children based on their age, sex and diversity. Morevoer they must as much as possible be defined taking into account the specificities of the context and - when appropriate - be built on existing coping mechanisms. 3) Appropriate is related to the physical safety and psychosocial well-being of the child. Specific attention should be put on non-discrimination of fostered children compared to biological ones. 4) Unaccompanied and/or separated children must be disaggegated by age and sex. This indicator excludes the reunification of other family members (above 18) which is to be reported under PRO-R14"

title.narrative: WSH-R4 Water supply

description.narrative: "Functional drainage: no substantial presence of stagnant water in and around the settlement, whether as a large body of standing water (such as a pond) or a high density of small areas (such as water standing in tyre tracks). If the standing water is contaminated by wastewater then even small quantities are significant. Small puddles of rainwater that dry up after a day or so should not be considered a substantial presence. Distance: Standing water that is at least 30m from living areas is effectively outside the perimeter of the settlement. Gradient: Site gradient should not exceed 6%, unless extensive drainage and erosion control measures are taken, or be less than 1% to provide for adequate drainage. Drainage channels may still be required to minimise flooding or ponding. Water table: Lowest point of the site should be not less than 3 metres above the estimated maximum level of the water table."

title.narrative: CSH-R1 Unconditional and unrestricted cash

description.narrative: "Unconditional transfers are provided to beneficiaries without the recipient having to do anything in return in order to receive the assistance . Unrestricted transfers can be used entirely as the recipient chooses i.e. there are no restrictions on how the transfer is spent (Definitions of CALP). It can be delivered e.g. through local banks, shops, traders, local money transfer companies, remittance companies and post offices in either one or several instalments. Please include in the activity description the amount and frequency of cash transfers (i.e. how often). In case beneficiaries receive multiple transfers (e.g. each month), please only count the beneficiaries once. "
